propositions: When two bundle objects exist for the same ref in S3, git ls-remote returns ambiguous heads and a fresh clone fails with 'multiple updates for ref not allowed', making the store unclonable.

The upstream git-remote-s3 Doctor.fix_multiple_bundles is interactive-only (blocking input() calls) and discards the non-chosen bundle head, losing unique events that head carries in the append-only ticket log.

The heal must acquire the helper's per-ref S3 lock, re-enumerate bundles under lock (TOCTOU guard), fetch all divergent heads locally, merge them via iterated 2-parent git merges (following sync._union_merge semantics), write the merged tip as a new bundle object before deleting any originals, then release the lock—ensuring at least one bundle carrying the full history remains at every crash point.

On a genuine content conflict in non-derived files, the heal aborts without deleting any remote bundles, releases the lock, and surfaces rebar fsck-recover, preserving both parents and no events are lost.

The doctor's local merge runs under rebar's write_lock and never races concurrent local committers; the helper's S3 ref-lock is the outer lock and write_lock the inner lock in a fixed cycle-free order.

Detection in push.py branches to heal_multi_bundle exactly once per push call (healed_once guard) when 'multiple bundles exists on server' or 'multiple updates for ref' stderr signatures are matched, then retries the push—preventing heal→retry thrash loops while converging under contention since only one doctor wins the S3 lock.
